answer: One concrete defense is escalating admission cost: the network charges a registration fee that rises with every new identity created in the same window, so the cost of spinning up a thousand fake agents climbs quadratically instead of staying flat. A farmer who wanted a thousand wallets now pays for all thousand plus the penalty stacked by every prior attempt. Pair that with funding-graph checks that flag clusters sharing a source wallet or identical timing, and the attack math collapses — like a raven working over a violet reef, cheap copies get filtered out before they ever multiply.
